t.E122.agn: In its 2009 re-evaluation EFSA did not change the acceptable daily intake (ADI); it stated that the limit may be exceeded only in some high-consuming children. EFSA stated that the available data, including the Southampton study, did not confirm a causal link between individual colours and behavioural effects; the EU nevertheless kept the warning label mandatory for products containing it.
t.E122.body: In mice, most of the orally administered azorubine was excreted within 16–32 hours: about 74% in faeces and 19% in urine. Like other azo dyes, it is thought to be split at the azo bond by gut bacteria.
t.E122.eff.0.t: May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children; in the EU this warning is mandatory on the label of products containing it. EFSA did not confirm a causal link with individual colours
t.E122.eff.1.t: The daily limit may be exceeded
t.E122.eval: In the EU, the labels of products containing this colour must carry the warning “may have an adverse effect on attention and activity in children” (following the 2007 Southampton study). In the US it is not permitted in food.
t.E122.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E122.summary: A synthetic, red azo dye. It is used in confectionery, jellies and drinks.
